short_answer: Bryan Leonard is a real, long running handicapper. His WagerTalk bio says he has been a professional since 1984, moved from Cleveland to Las Vegas in 1997, and once wrote basketball and football newsletters. He sells every package through WagerTalk, a large Las Vegas pick store that publishes its terms and a seller address. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money over time is a separate question. WagerTalk shows streaks such as "44-26 NHL Run" and "104-66 CFB Run", a list of his last 20 picks, and Who's Hot boards for the last 3, 7 and 30 days. On 17 Nov 2026 his last 20 picks went 11 and 9. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick that we could check.

Independent buyer comment about him by name is almost absent. Forum users mostly pass his plays around, and the complaints we found are about WagerTalk as a whole, not about him. Treat him as an experienced seller with marketing numbers, not a proven winner.

guarantee: On WagerTalk the guarantee is an extra cost option. On 17 Nov 2026 his $5 NHL play cost $8 with it. The site says that if the daily package "does not result in an overall profit across all included plays," the paid cash value is "credited back to your account to be used on a future purchase." That is store credit, not cash.

The WagerTalk refund policy says "All Sales are Final and products are sold 'as is'" and that no refund is issued once a product is purchased, delivered or viewed. Nothing covers losses on the bets themselves, and those are usually far larger than the price of a pick.

claims_note: The bio stresses low volume, but the same page lists 20 picks over 14 to 16 Nov 2026, and the Who's Hot board showed him at 29 and 22 over the last 7 days in all sports. That is a busy schedule for a seller who calls himself selective.
The streak boxes do not say when each run starts. A run cut from a longer history tells you little; every handicapper has a hot stretch somewhere.

An older BetFirm profile, last modified in 2016 and now marked "Capper not found," described him as running Bryan Leonard Sports for 31 years and gave a 32 and 17 NFL run since late 2014. It is another seller page, not an audit, and it is old.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every Bryan Leonard pick with the line, the odds and the release time, no contest results we could open, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the seller publishes: WagerTalk lists his last 20 graded picks with odds and a result. On 17 Nov 2026 those 20 picks, from 14 to 16 Nov, went 11 wins and 9 losses, and all 4 of his NFL picks on 15 Nov lost. The Who's Hot boards showed him at 29 and 22 in all sports over the last 7 days, plus short winning runs in single sports. These are graded by the store that sells the picks, so they are marketing, not an audit.
His plays are copied by users into forum threads, but nobody we found keeps a long running independent tally.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Bryan Leonard pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Bryan Leonard performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the streaks on his WagerTalk profile run from about 58% to 63% winners. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Bryan Leonard is very thin. We found forum posts that copy his plays and reviews that criticize the WagerTalk store in general. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found no review, complaint or results thread about Bryan Leonard by name. On TheRX in 2026 and on the Bookmakers Review forum in 2024, users simply posted his plays next to other services, without saying whether they won money. TheRX now lists him, and all WagerTalk handicappers, among services members must not post. Reviews of WagerTalk itself on CapperTek from 2022 to 2026 are mostly negative, saying the store's experts lose and show only good stats, but none of them names him. Our archive of Reddit betting posts held nothing about him. We found no billing complaint and no praise from a buyer.

On the Bookmakers Review forum, a member posted his Friday college football best bet, a 4% play on UNLV, with a note that his 2024 college football record was 10 and 11 at that point. No one discussed the result.

In a TheRX service play thread, a member posted two of his plays, an NHL team total and a Dodgers run line. The thread header lists "All Wagertalk Cappers" and Bryan Leonard among services members are told not to post.

Several CapperTek reviews of WagerTalk say its handicappers lose overall and that the store shows only stats that look good. One reviewer in Jan 2026 listed six WagerTalk handicappers he followed for four months and said all lost. None of these reviews names Bryan Leonard, so they describe the store, not him.

We found no Sportsbook Review or Covers thread about his service, no Better Business Bureau profile, and no posts about him in our archive of r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting posts. An old CappersPicks page praising him is an affiliate page covered in sportsbook bonus codes, so we did not count it.

conflicts: WagerTalk sells his picks and keeps the record, the Hot Streaks and the Who's Hot board that promote them. The store has a direct interest in how he looks.
The guarantee is sold by the same store and pays in store credit, which keeps a losing buyer spending there.
Third party pages that praise him, such as CappersPicks, carry offshore sportsbook bonus codes. Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators.
strengths: A named handicapper with a long career he describes in detail, sold by a store with written terms and a Las Vegas address.
Every package has a published price, and WagerTalk shows his last 20 graded picks with odds.
Cheap ways to sample him, such as single plays on sale for $5.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a streak, a short board or a total chosen by the seller.
The guarantee costs extra and pays store credit, never cash, and all sales are final.
The bio says he releases only games he bets himself and favors quality over quantity, yet the profile lists about 20 plays in three days.
Contest wins and top finishes are claimed but mostly not named, and we could not check them.
The same football package shows two prices on one page ($449 special and $529 in the passes table).
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real handicapper with a long career, sold through WagerTalk, which publishes terms and a Las Vegas address. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because no full record of every pick is public, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Bryan Leonard cost?
On 17 Nov 2026 WagerTalk sold single plays on sale for $5, daily passes from $39, 30 days for $299 and one year for $1,999, with a one year special at $1,188. Season passes ran from $259 to $719.
Does Bryan Leonard have a verified record?

No. WagerTalk shows streaks, his last 20 picks and short leaderboards, all graded by the store that sells him. On 17 Nov 2026 his last 20 picks went 11 and 9. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

You get every play he releases in the window you buy, from a seller with decades in the business. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays. The optional guarantee pays only store credit, and nothing covers your betting losses.
